Government has failed to deliver on China promises, says BIST Committee. In Parliament's first official report on doing business with China (102 pages), published 2 November 2026, the BIST Committee warns that Government has failed to deliver on its 2024 promise of a new, strategic, long-term, consistent UK approach to China.
The Government has embarked on a course of re-engagement with China "without having finalised its China audit or published a strategy".
The Government's record of decision making on China – such as the 11th hour blocking of Ming Yang's £1.5 billion wind turbine factory investment on the grounds of unspecified national security concerns after years of negotiations, or the emergency takeover of British Steel from the firm's Chinese owners – has been characterised by "reactivity, inconsistency, and opacity".
Rt Hon Liam Byrne MP, chair of the BIST Committee, said: "Britain's businesses cannot plan for the future when the Government keeps making up its China policy as it goes along. Ministers promised clarity and consistency. Instead, we have opportunities missed, risks unmanaged and decisions left until the eleventh hour."
Byrne set out "clear new rules of the game: protect what Britain must control, manage the risks we can mitigate and back British firms where trade can grow", noting these rules "must have bite".
